title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope Declared 'Go for Launch,' Falcon Heavy Rolls to Pad 39A
detail: NASA and SpaceX completed a Launch Readiness Review on August 28, 2026 and declared the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope 'go for launch' atop a Falcon Heavy rocket, confirming the vehicle, observatory, ground systems, and weather outlook were ready to proceed into countdown. On August 29, the encapsulated observatory — mated to Falcon Heavy inside SpaceX's Launch Complex 39A hangar since August 24-25 — rolled out to the pad at Kennedy Space Center and was raised to vertical, with NASA holding a science briefing (9:00 a.m. EDT) and a prelaunch press conference (10:30 a.m. EDT) ahead of Sunday's attempt. Liftoff is targeted for 7:26 a.m. EDT on August 30 (backup: 7:22 a.m. EDT August 31), sending Roman roughly 1.5 million km to the Sun-Earth L2 halo orbit already home to the James Webb Space Telescope. Equipped with a 300-megapixel Wide Field Instrument covering 100x the sky area of Hubble in a single shot plus a coronagraph, Roman is expected to survey for dark matter and dark energy, map billions of galaxies, and could discover roughly 100,000 new exoplanets — more than every prior planet-hunting observatory combined. It is the sixth NASA flagship-class primary payload to fly on a SpaceX Falcon rocket from Kennedy, following IXPE, Psyche, GOES-U, Europa Clipper, and IMAP. The Space Launch Delta 45 Weather Squadron forecast a 60% chance of favorable conditions for Sunday, improving to 70% for a Monday backup attempt, with cumulus clouds and lightning the main watch items.

media.caption: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, encapsulated in its Falcon Heavy payload fairing, travels to SpaceX's Launch Complex 39A hangar at Kennedy Space Center ahead of its August 30, 2026 launch
